correctness.rationale: For all t>0, the 2-by-2 generalized eigenvalue calculation yields the sharp unrestricted upper bound; at t ≠1 all norming row directions have ab(a²−b²)≠0, and the two norm-one column constraints force a nonzero Birkhoff functional, ruling out equality. The explicit balanced pair attains equality at t=1. The exact Birkhoff parametrization and uniform fourth-root expansion are valid on the whole compact ratio range; J has a unique strict nondegenerate maximizer. The analytic implicit function theorem gives local uniqueness and the calculated first- and higher-order coefficients. Symbolic checks and 3,300 sampled consistency assertions reproduce critical algebra, but the continuous claims rely on the proof. No global exact closed form for the restricted constant is inferred from finite checks.

value.rationale: The new theorem directly addresses the structural problem of whether Birkhoff-constrained norming pairs can realize the known unrestricted skew arithmetic mean. It gives a complete global equality-versus-strictness classification for every positive weight, identifies the exact leading price paid for the constraint, and rigorously computes the cubic local profile with one moving extremizing orbit. The simultaneous global rigidity and sharp local coefficient information are meaningful for this canonical Banach-space geometric constant; they are not a relabeling, an arbitrary finite slice, or merely a known norm value.
